def isPermutation(n: list[int], m: list[int]) -> bool:
    if len(n) != len(m):
        return False
    
    # Sort both arrays using only addition/subtraction (bubble sort)
    a = n[:]
    b = m[:]
    
    # Sort first array
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(len(a) - 1 - i):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                # Swap using only addition/subtraction
                a[j] = a[j] + a[j + 1]
                a[j + 1] = a[j] - a[j + 1]
                a[j] = a[j] - a[j + 1]
    
    # Sort second array
    for i in range(len(b)):
        for j in range(len(b) - 1 - i):
            if b[j] > b[j + 1]:
                # Swap using only addition/subtraction
                b[j] = b[j] + b[j + 1]
                b[j + 1] = b[j] - b[j + 1]
                b[j] = b[j] - b[j + 1]
    
    # Compare sorted arrays
    for i in range(len(a)):
        if a[i] != b[i]:
            return False
    return True


def main():
    # Test 1: Simple permutation
    print(isPermutation([1, 2, 3], [3, 1, 2]))
    
    # Test 2: Different lengths
    print(isPermutation([1, 2, 3], [1, 2]))
    
    # Test 3: Empty arrays
    print(isPermutation([], []))
    
    # Test 4: Same elements, different counts
    print(isPermutation([1, 1, 2], [1, 2, 2]))
    
    # Test 5: Zero values and negatives
    print(isPermutation([0, -1, 5], [5, 0, -1]))
    
    # Test 6: Single element
    print(isPermutation([42], [42]))
    
    # Test 7: Not a permutation
    print(isPermutation([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2, 3, 5]))
    
    # Test 8: Large values
    print(isPermutation([1000, 2000, 3000], [3000, 1000, 2000]))
    
    # Test 9: Duplicate elements permutation
    print(isPermutation([1, 2, 2, 3], [2, 1, 3, 2]))
    
    # Test 10: Boundary - maximum integer values
    print(isPermutation([2147483647, -2147483648], [-2147483648, 2147483647]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
